newsitem.title: LEBANON: FOCUS-Banque Audi buys Beirut bank.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Banque Audi buys Beirut bank.

text.p: Banque Audi announced on Thursday the acquisition of medium-sized Credit Commercial du Moyen-Orient (CCMO) in Lebanon's second bank takeover in a week.

Financial sources said Audi, one of Lebanon's biggest and most dynamic banks, paid $50 million for CCMO which has eight branches, assets of 390 billion Lebanese pounds ($253 million) and a 0.85 percent market share.
Audi is one of three banks listed on the fledgling Beirut Stock Exchange and its shares are regarded by many brokers as the 10-share market's blue chip stock.
It said in a statement it had acquired all CCMO's shares and the two banks would eventually be fully merged. CCMO Chairman Georges Achi would join Banque Audi's board, it added.
The takeover followed the acquisition last week of Banque Geagea, a small, family-owned bank, by Societe Generale Libano-Europeene de Banque, one of Lebanon's top 10 banks.
Completion of the two takeovers will reduce the overcrowded Lebanese banking sector to 70 active banks.

Audi bought CCMO after losing out to a Saudi billionaire last week in bidding for Credit Libanais, a medium-sized bank with the biggest branch network in the country that was sold by the central bank.
Freddie Baz, a director of Banque Audi, told Reuters CCMO was a very healthy bank with high financial standing.
"This is a real consolidation for the banking sector because you can talk of economies of scale and upsizing," he said.
Beirut financiers said the acquisition was a welcome move towards banking sector consolidation, but some believed Audi may have paid a high price.
"It's a good acquisition but at a high price," said a banker who asked not to be identified.
"They wanted to take Credit Libanais but when that failed they had this offer."
Another financier, Bassam Yammine of Lebanon Invest finance house, said the takeover was good for Lebanon's banking system.

"We need consolidation. We need some of the smaller, the small-to-medium banks, to be willing to sell," Yammine said. "I believe you will see more of this because medium-sized banks are beginning to feel the heat and the banking sector is beginning to shake up due to reduced interest rates and margins and increasing costs.
"All the big banks are trying to position themselves well and that's why I think you'll hear of other banks trying to do the same thing," Yammine added.

Yammine said CCMO had good senior management and the acquisition could be profitable to Audi from the viewpoint of efficiency, "but the question is how much they can retain of CCMOs business," he added.
